agent.name: Silver-Milk Team Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: Dated technology-landscape intelligence: eight fixed landscape dimensions (capability, use cases, trackers, ecosystem, standards, price/performance, coverage, alternatives) each with a basis, broad signals separated from the few that matter to this organization, execution gates kept apart from landscape signals, a gating-condition x movement table that sets the monitoring stance, owned triggers mapped to actions, and a dated stale/hype flag (never the adoption decision, never a vendor selection)

analytical_question: Where do text-to-image diffusion models and their application to disposable internal concept boards sit in the landscape, and which external developments should the retailer monitor during its six-week evidence review?
general_et_finding:
AS OF: 2026-11-17
UNIT: Text-to-image diffusion models, with latent diffusion as the historical reference architecture.
L1 TECHNICAL CAPABILITY: Insufficient evidence — controlled evaluations document composition and attribute-binding failures, but the retrieved evidence does not establish reliability on bounded real tasks (Huang et al., 2025-02). BASIS: E1.
L2 USE-CASE EVIDENCE: Use cases emerging — a provider documents Stable Diffusion embedded in a live software workflow, with no independent multi-organization replication retrieved (Stability AI, 2025-09). BASIS: E2.
L3 TRACKER PLACEMENT: Not covered by Thoughtworks Technology Radar in the inspected volumes 34 and 35. Neither edition provides a category placement or a basis for movement (Thoughtworks, 2026-04; 2026-11). BASIS: E3, E4.
L4 VENDOR/ECOSYSTEM STRUCTURE: Insufficient evidence — integration deals and managed and open-weight distribution show multiple delivery routes, with no category-wide evidence of platform dominance or concentration (WIRED, 2026-04; Black Forest Labs, 2025-11). BASIS: E5, E6.
L5 STANDARDS & REGULATION: Emerging — U.S. copyright analysis addresses generative outputs broadly. The cited report is agency interpretation and identifies no binding technical requirement specific to this architecture (U.S. Copyright Office, 2025-01). BASIS: E7.
L6 PRICE/PERFORMANCE: Insufficient evidence — launch pricing does not establish a 12-month change at equivalent capability (Black Forest Labs, 2025-11). BASIS: E6.
L7 COVERAGE TONE: Mixed — release coverage emphasizes creative capabilities, while reporting on ecosystem growth also describes safeguard controversy (VentureBeat, 2025-11; WIRED, 2026-04). BASIS: E5, E8.
L8 ALTERNATIVES & COMPLEMENTS: INCUMBENT: human-led visual development with design software and existing images. COMPETING: autoregressive image synthesis and instruction-based editors outside the category. COMPLEMENTS: curated reference assets, image-editing software and human review.
POSITION: Bounded benchmarks and a reported live integration show practical capabilities. Evidence remains limited on real-task reliability, breadth of production use and comparable cost trends.
application_finding:
APPLICATION SIGNALS: L1 matters because concepts must remain interpretable and preserve recognizable reference features when required. L2 matters because real board workflows reveal iteration and review work that demonstrations omit. L6 matters because the useful cost unit is a board accepted for internal review, including retries and human time.
APPLICATION-SPECIFIC EVIDENCE: Thin — product-identity editing research addresses a relevant subtask. No independently verified end-to-end comparison for disposable internal campaign concept boards was retrieved.
STRONGEST ALTERNATIVE: Human-led visual development with design software and existing images — it gives reviewers direct control over layout and reference fidelity and provides a measurable workflow baseline.
organization_specific_finding:
UNIT OF ANALYSIS: The hypothetical U.S. homeware retailer's decision about preparing a bounded comparison for internal concept boards.
GATING CONDITION: Given its fast-follower posture, stocked catalog and existing review workflow, the retailer needs documented reference-based options and credible comparable evidence that required product details can be preserved at a measurable cost per reviewed board.
CONDITION STATUS: Partly met — a reference-based option is documented, while comparable evidence on catalog fidelity and reviewed-board cost is missing. BASIS: E6, E9, E10.
MOVEMENT: None — benchmark gains on adjacent editing tasks do not establish durable progress on the combined fidelity and workflow-cost condition. BASIS: E6, E9.
STANCE: Scheduled watch.
EXECUTION GATES: Exact provider and plan terms, retention and security review — security/procurement review, individual owner not stated. Catalog input and output rights clearance — owner not stated. Separate trial authorization — owner not stated.
RELEVANT SIGNALS: L1 — measured product-detail errors matter because staff would work from catalog photos. L4 — managed and open-weight delivery routes make integration and portability worth comparing because procurement leads software selection. L5 — output copyright interpretation makes intended reuse relevant because downstream customers see approved assets. L6 — missing comparable pricing makes per-board workflow costs important because the retailer has a budget and no matched baseline.
POPULAR BUT NOT DECISIVE HERE: Black Forest Labs funding and distribution deals do not measure fit with the catalog workflow.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL DEVELOPMENT: L1 — the June 2026 ProductConsistency evaluation isolates product-identity errors. Its findings make fidelity a criterion for deciding whether the evidence warrants preparing a bounded comparison.
ECOSYSTEM DEPENDENCY: The model distribution interface that determines which reference inputs, settings and versions can be reproduced when switching deployment routes.
OPTIONS DOCUMENTED: FLUX.2 [dev] — Black Forest Labs documents open weights and multi-reference editing (vendor-claim, E6). Firefly Structure Reference — Adobe documents reference-guided layout in its web app (vendor-claim, E11). NO SELECTION.

evidence.claim: E1: T2I-CompBench++ evaluates named text-to-image diffusion models on composition, including attribute binding and spatial relations, using controlled prompts.
evidence.source_or_reference: Huang et al., T2I-CompBench++: An Enhanced and Comprehensive Benchmark for Compositional Text-to-Image Generation. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40031217/
evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run. SOURCE CLASS: independent. LOAD-BEARING for L1. Controlled results do not measure end-to-end performance in a real workflow.

evidence.source_or_reference: Stability AI, HubSpot Scales Image Generation 150% with Stability AI in Amazon Bedrock. https://stability.ai/customer-stories/hubspot-scales-image-generation-150-with-stability-ai-in-amazon-bedrock

evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run. SOURCE CLASS: industry-analyst. LOAD-BEARING for L3.

evidence.notes: STATUS: inspected-this-run. SOURCE CLASS: industry-analyst. LOAD-BEARING for L3.

evidence.source_or_reference: Supplied case context, capabilities_constraints, risk_consequence_context and time_horizon.

evidence.source_or_reference: Adobe, New Structure Reference Capabilities in Adobe Firefly Bring a New Level of Creative Control to Ideation. https://blog.adobe.com/en/publish/2024/03/26/new-structure-reference-capabilities-adobe-firefly-bring-new-level-of-creative-control-ideation

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: COMPETING READING: Background scan — a stricter interpretation would require documented catalog-like workflow economics before counting any part of the external condition as met. Available reference tooling supports partial status here because it satisfies the option-availability component.
CHASM EVIDENCE FOR: Stability AI's September 2025 HubSpot case describes a named diffusion model family embedded in a live software offering. It is a single supplier-reported deployment (E2).

CHASM EVIDENCE AGAINST: Huang et al.'s February 2025 controlled evaluation documents composition challenges for named diffusion models. It provides task-level counterevidence to claims of routine reliability, with no estimate of production prevalence (E1).

DISTINGUISHING EVIDENCE: Dated, independently audited records from recurring catalog-based concept-board workflows that identify the architecture and compare required detail preservation and total cost per reviewed board with a matched manual baseline.

STALE/HYPE FLAG: Black Forest Labs' 2025-11-25 claim of best available product consistency with multi-reference FLUX.2 inputs (E6) is a launch comparison without independently verified catalog workflow performance. CONTROL: Used the release to establish documented features only and excluded its performance claim from movement. REFRESH BY: 2026-12-11.

The case does not supply a third-party market claim to trace. Retrieved evidence does not establish category-wide market concentration, a normalized price trend or routine production use. The preliminary product-editing study is relevant to the application and is kept outside the category-level capability rating.
confidence_and_uncertainty: CONFIDENCE: Moderate — broad landscape confidence is moderate for benchmark limitations and documented delivery routes, and low for pricing, concentration and routine production. Local relevance is well supported for reference fidelity and review workload by the case facts, with low confidence in actual workflow economics. No applicable category placement was verified from Gartner, IEEE Computer Society, Forrester or IDC. Independent multi-organization production studies, comparable adopter workflow records and matched price/performance series were not retrieved.
value_opportunity_implication: Reference-based generation could widen the range of concepts available for internal review. The retailer's existing catalog and creative workflow give it a baseline for measuring that benefit. Time spent preparing references, correcting details, reviewing rejected outputs and moving assets between tools can materially affect cost per usable board.
risk_governance_implication: Prioritize reference fidelity and total review effort in the workflow comparison, and examine integration and switching costs by deployment route. Security/procurement review must clear applicable plan terms and retention before any catalog input is used. Catalog rights and authorization require separate clearance. Human review and independently checked final product photography limit downstream exposure.
recommendation_management_implication: STANCE: Scheduled watch — WATCH FIRST: independently documented product-reference fidelity in recurring creative work, with reviewer time and integration effort visible in the reported cost. STRONGEST ALTERNATIVE: Human-led visual development with design software and existing images. REFRESH: Review the evidence on 2026-12-11 within the six-week horizon, then quarterly if the stance remains the same. Refresh the full source register at least annually.
change_monitoring_triggers: TRIGGER 1 [L2] USE-CASE: By 2026-12-11, an independent audit of a recurring catalog-based internal concept-board workflow reports acceptable product fidelity and lower total cost per reviewed board against matched manual work, threshold pending creative operations lead approval — SOURCE: published workflow audit with its comparison method — OWNER: creative operations lead (proposed) — CADENCE: weekly through the review → Landscape not the constraint

TRIGGER 2 [L1] CAPABILITY: By 2026-12-11, an independent matched evaluation reports reproducible improvement in preserving required product details across documented reference-based options, threshold pending creative operations lead approval — SOURCE: independent benchmark report with released methods — OWNER: creative operations lead (proposed) — CADENCE: weekly through the review → Active watch, to inspect the method and scope a local test for the Adoption Agent

TRIGGER 3 [L4] REVERSAL: By 2026-12-11, an independent ecosystem inventory verifies that no documented multi-reference option remains obtainable through the managed or open-weight deployment routes under review — SOURCE: independent availability inventory backed by endpoint and release histories — OWNER: procurement reviewer (proposed) — CADENCE: weekly through the review → Background scan
abstention_or_more_information_needed: MORE INFO → matched workflow evidence: Comparable board briefs, required product details, manual and freelance effort, review time and rework would make the cost and fidelity findings interpretable.
MORE INFO → ownership of execution gates: The case names review functions but does not identify who can clear catalog input rights, verify retention and authorize the trial.
HANDOFF → Creation Agent: Which architectural changes led from latent diffusion to current text-conditioned diffusion and reference-guided systems?
HANDOFF → Innovation Agent: What lifecycle and degree of innovation apply to internal concept-board work?
HANDOFF → Promethean Agent: What significance class is supported for this bounded use?
HANDOFF → Diffusion Agent: What diffusion stage and timing are supported for the defined category?
HANDOFF → Adoption Agent: Does the evidence support preparing a bounded comparison, and what design could distinguish workflow benefit from added review effort?
HANDOFF → Organizational Adoption Agent: Can the retailer govern and run the workflow, and who can clear each outstanding execution gate?
